traits.build_notes: ALL NUMBERS ARE ESTIMATES, not values read from a study in this session (full texts could not be opened): typical magnitudes of international opposites on FIVB rosters (self-reported reaches, often generous), standing reach ~1.31 x stature (the app's default), spike reach ~ standing reach + 0.93 m (men) / + 0.68 m (women) / + 0.57 m (U16 girls), block reach ~ standing reach + 0.73 / 0.56 / 0.44 m; U16 values are for selected/competitive club or regional players. Supporting evidence: Palao et al. 2014 (Olympic and World Championship rosters 2000-2012) found height, spike reach and block reach differ by position, with opposites, outside hitters and middles the attackers/blockers; Slovenian female opposites: arm span relates more strongly than height to spike and block reach; Indonesian club men averaged ~3.21 m spike and ~3.11 m block reach (well below international level). Build: among the tallest players on the team (typically a little shorter than the middles, similar to or taller than the outside hitters), long arms (arm span about 1.02-1.05 x stature), powerful and often the heaviest hitter, strong trunk rotators and shoulders because the opposite attacks from front and back row (D/pipe from zone 1) and is the main scorer out of system. Gear: standard team jersey and shorts (not the libero's contrasting jersey), knee pads (often low-profile; some elite men play without), ankle braces common, sometimes a compression sleeve or tape on the hitting shoulder/arm and finger tape for blocking. Handedness: left-handed opposites are common because the set reaches their hitting side first; their attack and approach postures equal a mirrored right-handed outside hitter, while block, defence, cover and transition postures are position-defined and must NOT be mirrored; serves can be mirrored.

techniques.name: Medium ready (right side)
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: Balanced medium posture the opposite holds in right-front/right-back base before the play develops: feet a little wider than the shoulders, right (sideline) foot slightly ahead so the body faces a touch toward the court, knees ~60 deg, chest over the knees, hands relaxed in front at waist height and eyes up. Weight on the balls of the feet so the first step can go in any direction. Position-defined, not hand-defined: use it unmirrored for a left-handed opposite.
techniques.confidence: estimated (from coaching descriptions of the medium/ready posture and anatomy; no study measured an opposite's ready stance)

techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: Low defensive base in zone 1 when the opponent attacks: wide stance (~0.65 m), right foot forward, knees ~85-90 deg, trunk inclined ~35 deg with a flat back, arms out in front and apart, head up to read the hitter. The body is turned slightly toward the court so a dig is angled back to the middle. Position-defined, not hand-defined: use it unmirrored for a left-handed opposite.

techniques.name: Free-ball release ready
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: On a free-ball call the front-row opposite releases from the net to the approach start (about 3.5-4 m off the net, just inside the right sideline) and stands medium-high, opened toward the court and the setter so the pass and set can be seen, arms loose, ready to start the approach with the left foot. For a left-handed opposite the release spot is usually a little wider (outside the sideline) and the body opens the same way (toward the setter).

techniques.name: Transition off the net (right side)
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: After landing from a block the opposite drops the right (outside) foot back, opens the hips and chest to the left toward the court to keep sight of the ball, and runs/shuffles back to the approach start near the right sideline. Key instant: just after the drop step - right foot back, pelvis ~45 deg open to the court, chest turned further toward the ball, knees bent and arms relaxed.

techniques.name: Right-side approach start (first step)
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: First, directional step (left foot) of a right-handed opposite's 3-step left-right-left approach. The opposite starts near the right sideline around 3.5-4 m from the net and runs fairly straight at the net (often a few degrees inward, 'body moving toward the middle'), with the chest and hips slightly open to the left to watch the set travel from the setter; this is flatter and narrower than an outside hitter's banana approach because the ball has to cross in front of the body to reach the right shoulder. Left-handed opposite: do not use the automatic mirror of this posture (that is a left-hander hitting from zone 4); a lefty opposite moves like a mirrored right-handed outside hitter - the set arrives on the hitting side, the approach comes from outside the right sideline at roughly 30-45 deg and the hips open toward the setter.
techniques.confidence: estimated (coaching texts on right-side approach angle and footwork; no measured opposite-specific approach angles found)

techniques.name: Penultimate (big) step - right foot plant
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: Instant the right heel strikes at the end of the long penultimate step (~1 m): trunk inclined forward, both arms swung fully back and high behind the body, left toes just leaving the floor, eyes up on the set. techniques.name: Take-off plant (deepest knee bend)
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: Both feet planted (left foot slightly ahead and turned in), knees at their deepest bend (~72 deg flexion, i.e. ~107 deg knee angle) while the arms swing down past the hips and forward, trunk inclined, chest just starting to turn right. For a right-handed opposite the hips stay nearly square or slightly open to the setter rather than closed, so the ball can cross in front of the face before contact. A 2026 position study found opposites have the largest propulsive knee range (~73 deg) of all pin hitters. Left-handed opposite: do not use the automatic mirror of this posture (that is a left-hander hitting from zone 4); a lefty opposite moves like a mirrored right-handed outside hitter - the set arrives on the hitting side, the approach comes from outside the right sideline at roughly 30-45 deg and the hips open toward the setter.
techniques.confidence: estimated, anchored to measured knee data (Frontiers in Physiology 2026: opposites' propulsive knee range 72.8 +/- 9.3 deg; the ~107 deg minimum knee angle is an abstract value whose group label is ambiguous); other joints estimated

techniques.name: Arm cock (bow-and-arrow), right side
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: Rising in the air: left arm reaches up toward the ball, right elbow pulled back and high (above shoulder level), hand behind the head, back arched and the chest turned ~30 deg to the right of the net while the pelvis stays slightly open to the setter ('open hip'); legs bent behind in a bow. Max layback follows a few milliseconds later: studies report peak external rotation of 160 +/- 10 deg (Reeser) - the 115 deg used here is the recognisable bow-and-arrow frame; use 150-160 for a max-layback frame. Men tend to show more torso rotation in the backswing (Prosch). Left-handed opposite: do not use the automatic mirror of this posture (that is a left-hander hitting from zone 4); a lefty opposite moves like a mirrored right-handed outside hitter - the set arrives on the hitting side, the approach comes from outside the right sideline at roughly 30-45 deg and the hips open toward the setter.
techniques.confidence: estimated, anchored to measured peak shoulder external rotation (Reeser 2010: 160 +/- 10 deg) and qualitative sex differences (Prosch); trunk and leg values estimated

techniques.name: Open-hip forward arm swing (opposite)
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: Opposite-specific frame between max layback and contact on a set that travels from the setter on the hitter's left across to the right shoulder: the pelvis stays open toward the setter/court while the chest unwinds from right to left, the right elbow leads high in front of the shoulder with the forearm still vertical, the left arm pulls down to the chest and the trunk starts to side-bend left. This open-hip swing lets a right-hander hit both the line and the sharp cross ('cut') from the right side. Left-handed opposite: do not use the automatic mirror of this posture (that is a left-hander hitting from zone 4); a lefty opposite moves like a mirrored right-handed outside hitter - the set arrives on the hitting side, the approach comes from outside the right sideline at roughly 30-45 deg and the hips open toward the setter.
techniques.confidence: estimated (4-phase spike model - approach, arm cocking, arm acceleration, follow-through - as used by Reeser et al. 2010; opposite-specific hip/chest timing from coaching texts)

techniques.name: Spike contact from the right side (cross-court)
techniques.handedness: right (assume a right-handed player; mirror is automatic - see the left-handed note in the description)
techniques.description: Ball contact at near-full reach above and slightly in front of the right shoulder: hitting arm almost straight (elbow ~34 deg), shoulder elevated ~130 deg relative to the trunk while the trunk side-bends ~20 deg to the left so the arm is close to vertical in space, wrist starting to snap, left arm tucked to the chest, chest already rotated a little left of the pelvis for the cross-court/cut shot, legs flexing forward under the body. Hitting-arm note: shoulder values are given for the app's Euler order (abduction applied before flexion); this flex-dominant overhead arm with a negative ext_rot is exactly the same rotation as the abduction-dominant form flex ~-20 / abd ~130-150 / ext_rot ~105-125 in this rig, which is closer to how the studies report it (abduction ~130 deg at contact). Left-handed opposite: do not use the automatic mirror of this posture (that is a left-hander hitting from zone 4); a lefty opposite moves like a mirrored right-handed outside hitter - the set arrives on the hitting side, the approach comes from outside the right sideline at roughly 30-45 deg and the hips open toward the setter.
